response: Dokdo, also known as Takeshima in Japan and Liancourt Rocks, is a group of islets located in the Sea of Japan. It consists of two main islets, East Islet (Seogdo) and West Islet (Dokdo), and numerous smaller rocks. Currently, Dokdo is under the jurisdiction of Ulleung County, North Gyeongsang Province, South Korea. There are permanent residents living on Dokdo, mainly working as village chiefs and coast guards. Therefore, it is not entirely accurate to call Dokdo an uninhabited island, as it does have a small number of permanent residents. However, the population is very small compared to typical inhabited islands.
